Guinea Women 15th Match, Group A United Arab Emirates Women vs Sri Lanka Women 16th Match, Group A ICC Board Meeting Jay Shah re-elected as ICC Chair
 by Cricbuzz Staff •     Share Tweet Jay Shah has been elected unopposed © AFP Jay Shah has been elected unopposed © AFP Jay Shah has been re-elected unopposed as chair of the International Cricket Council (ICC) on Sunday. At the Board meeting, which concluded in Bali, ICC members cited the need for continuity and stability in the organisation. Considering these factors, his name was proposed and approved by the members for another three-year term.
 Shah, who is currently into his second year as ICC chair, will thus continue in the position until December 2030. He assumed office in December 2024, which means his first three-year term runs until December 2027, with his second term beginning thereafter and culminating in December 2030.
 As per the ICC Constitution, an ICC chair can serve a maximum of two terms of three years each.
 “The decision reflects the Board’s confidence in Shah’s leadership and provides continuity at a defining moment for the sport, with global expansion, growth in fandom and commercial development central to its strategic roadmap. Cricket is also preparing for its return to the Olympic Games at Los Angeles 2028 and has recently announced an expanded long-range programme for competitions, delivering greater participation and development pathways,” the ICC said in a statement.
 Accepting the endorsement, Shah said, “Serving as Chair of the ICC is both a privilege and a responsibility, and I remain committed to working with our Members to advance the interests of cricket across the world. I have always believed that cricket’s greatest strength lies in its ability to bring people together. With the support of the Board and our Members, our focus will be on turning ambition into action and ensuring that the progress we make leaves a lasting legacy for generations to come.”
 England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) Richard Thompson said, “Balancing the traditions of our game with the opportunities presented by innovation, new audiences and changing commercial dynamics will be critical in the years ahead. The ICC has an important role to play in bringing Members together to shape this future and establish a sustainable direction for international cricket.
 “I congratulate Jay on his continued appointment and look forward to working with him and fellow Members as we navigate this important next phase for the game.”
